name: Eiffel Tower

phases.title: The foundations
phases.text: Masonry blocks receive each of the four feet. Near the Seine, the digging goes on in compressed-air caissons, below the water line.

moments.title: Sixteen stone blocks
moments.text: Each leg stands on four blocks, one per edge: sixteen blocks built in five months.

moments.title: Digging under the Seine
moments.text: On the river side, workers dig below the water line, sheltered by watertight iron caissons.

phases.title: The four legs rise
phases.text: Parts arrive from the works already drilled. Above 30 m, twelve timber scaffolds hold up the leaning legs, then four 45 m ones carry the girders of the first floor, reached at 57 m.

moments.title: Everything is made in the works
moments.text: Every part is calculated, drawn, cut, drilled and pre-assembled at Levallois-Perret. A faulty part goes back to the workshop.

moments.title: One rivet, four men
moments.text: The first heats the rivet, the second holds it, the third shapes the head, the fourth strikes it with a sledgehammer. Two thirds of the rivets are fitted in the works.

moments.title: Cranes that climb
moments.text: On each leg, a small 3-tonne steam crane climbs with the tower, on the rails of the future lifts.

moments.title: A junction to the millimetre
moments.text: The first-floor girders rest on sandboxes that are slowly emptied. At the foot of two legs, hydraulic jacks correct a few centimetres.

phases.title: The second floor
phases.text: The legs draw together and meet. The second floor is reached at 115 m on 14 August 1888.

moments.title: 150 to 300 workers
moments.text: Thanks to prefabrication, 150 to 300 workers are enough to assemble every part on site.

phases.title: The top
phases.text: Above the second floor, a single column rises to 300 m.

moments.title: Thousands of drawings
moments.text: The design office produces 700 engineering drawings and 3,600 workshop plans for the 18,038 parts.

moments.title: 1,665 steps
moments.text: On 31 March 1889, Gustave Eiffel climbs the 1,665 steps from the esplanade to the top, the day the tower is inaugurated.

phases.title: The tower lights up
phases.text: Since 31 December 1985, 336 lamps set inside the structure light it in gold. Since 2000, 20,000 bulbs make it sparkle.

evidence.identity: Eiffel Tower (Tour Eiffel), Champ de Mars, 5 Avenue Anatole France, 75007 Paris, France (OSM way 5013364)

sources.read: The tower was built for the 1889 World's Fair: works started 26 January 1887, first floor 1 April 1888, second 14 August 1888, top 31 March 1889 (2 years, 2 months, 5 days). Square base 125 m across, 18,038 parts, 2,500,000 rivets, four lattice girders joined at the top; 150-300 workers; rivets set by teams of four; sandboxes and hydraulic jacks aligned the first-floor girders to a millimetre; caissons with compressed air on the Seine side; Sauvestre's monumental arches at the base were kept.

Sixteen stone blocks, one per tower edge, built in five months in masonry; 700 engineering drawings and 3,600 workshop plans for the 18,000 parts; prefabrication at Levallois-Perret with defective parts sent back; two thirds of the rivets set at the factory; wooden scaffolds and 3-tonne steam cranes that climbed the legs; the second floor was reached in July 1888 and the 300 m summit in March 1889.

The secret of the 22-month assembly was complete prefabrication: 12,000 parts calculated, drawn, cut, drilled and pre-assembled in the Levallois-Perret works; 150 to 300 workers; sixteen masonry foundation blocks, one per edge, with caissons under two pillars near the Seine; the first floor was the critical moment, aligned with sandboxes and hydraulic jacks.
674 steps lead from the ground to the second floor and 1,665 in total from the esplanade to the top; the stairway above the second floor is not open to the public and climbs the south leg.

Sandboxes and hydraulic cylinders at the base of two columns, driven by a hand pump, raised or lowered the first-floor beams by a few centimetres so the rivet holes met; the cylinders were removed and replaced by permanent wedges once the first floor was assembled.

Since 31 December 1985, 336 sodium spotlights inside the structure light the tower in gold; since 2000, 20,000 6W bulbs make it sparkle five minutes at the start of every hour; a rotating beacon sits on top; the monument has been illuminated since 1889 (gaslights).
Technical dimensions of the tower: foundations, floors at 57.63/115.73/276.13 m with sides 70.69/40.96/18.65 m, 125x125 m base, 74.24 m inner and 124.90 m outer gap between the piers, 1665 steps.

references.view: east, from the Bir-Hakeim bridge over the Seine
north, along the fountains of the Trocadero gardens

features.text: Four curved legs of lattice girders rising from a 125 m square base to meet at 300 m.
Three public platforms: the first at 57.63 m (70.69 m side), the second at 115.73 m (40.96 m side), the third at 276.13 m (18.65 m side).
Monumental semicircular arches linking the legs and the first level, kept from Sauvestre's design.
Wrought-iron lattice of riveted parts, 18,038 pieces and 2.5 million rivets, painted brown.
Golden lighting of 336 spotlights inside the structure since 31 December 1985, and 20,000 bulbs that make the tower sparkle since 2000.
Sixteen masonry foundation blocks, one below each edge of the four iron piers.
Every iron part was calculated, cut, drilled and pre-assembled at Levallois-Perret before reaching the site.
Twelve timber scaffolds first held the leaning legs, followed by four 45 m scaffold towers below the first floor.

evidence.geometry: Base and floor heights from the official figures (125 m square, 57.63/115.73/276.13 m, 300 m); the outline is OpenStreetMap way 5013364 traced to local metres; the lattice legs, decks and base arches are drawn with the profile of the real tower.

gaps: The model's four legs reach 87 m from the centre as the outline does, but the ground plan between the legs is wrong: in the sectors between two legs the model bulges 20-24 m too far (73 m where the outline measures 49 m), and at the four diagonal mid-points it falls short of the outline's bulges (39-44 m measured, 2-23 m modelled).
The first-floor deck overhung the legs by 3 m; the real floor is 70.69 m across, flush with the legs.
The base arches started 14 m above the ground with a 31 m span; on the tower they spring from the ground and crown near the first floor (74.24 m inner gap).
fixed: Deck overhangs set to the real floor widths (70.69 / 40.96 / 18.65 m).
Base arches lowered to the ground (base 0, rise 37 m, span 74.24 m) and the legs narrowed to 18 m, then measured again.
After measuring every combination, the original arch and leg widths were restored: they fix more sectors than any alternative tried.

gaps: The diagonal sectors between the legs still read 12-20 m too wide against the outline, and the diagonal bulges between the legs remain under-covered.
The phase strip reads correctly: foundations, the four legs with their scaffolds, the two platforms, the top and the night lighting.
Against the photos the proportions hold: the legs meet the first floor at 57.63 m, the second at 115.73 m and the top at 300 m.
remaining: The lattice is schematic: the real tower has several hundred lattice members per panel; the model keeps the silhouette and the panel rhythm.
The gap between the model and the measured outline is 8.2 m at the 90th percentile, concentrated in the sectors between the legs; see evidence.uncertainties.

uncertainties: The lattice is schematic: the real tower has several hundred lattice members per panel; the model keeps the silhouette and the panel rhythm.
The lifts, restaurants and the 2022 antenna (330 m) are left out.
The climbing steam crane and scaffold cage follow the documented construction method, while their exact position within the selected leg is interpretive.

The model's ground plan still differs from the OpenStreetMap outline in the sectors between the legs: the tower's piers are drawn as square lattice boxes, while the real piers are rounded and the space between them follows the base arches; the 90th-percentile gap is 8.2 m (max 23.6 m).

modelNote: Measured from the OpenStreetMap plan and the official dimensions (125 m base, 57.63/115.73/276.13 m floors, 300 m top); the lattice is simplified to its four legs, three floors and base arches, and the illumination is schematic.
